task.title: Stop board columns self-scrolling: disable scroll anchoring on task lists
task.description:
A status column that a user has scrolled creeps further down on its own with every one-second poll, and reaches the bottom without anyone touching it. Reported 2026-08-06; reproduced and root-caused the same day at commit c453596.

This ticket is now scoped to the immediate, unblocked mitigation. The structural fix is WB-01KZC3PGA0QCXKDQ936VPM67D5, which removes the cause and also cures two related defects; it depends on the queue correctness work and will take longer. Ship this first so users stop losing their place.

## Reproduction

Served the projects own board and drove real Chrome 151 headless over CDP. The DONE column held 37 tasks (clientHeight 635, scrollHeight 9189). Scrolled it to 35 percent, then sampled scrollTop once per poll:

  t+1.1s 3145   t+2.2s 3221   t+3.3s 3297   t+4.4s 3373   t+5.5s 3466
  t+6.6s 3559   t+7.7s 3635   t+8.8s 3729   t+9.9s 3823   t+11.0s 3916

Monotonic, about 76 to 93 px per tick, roughly a third of a card height. Nothing was interacting with the page.

## Root cause

Browser scroll anchoring reacting to wholesale DOM replacement. render() rebuilds each column with list.replaceChildren(fragment) on every poll (internal/webui/assets/index.html:1806-1808, driven by setInterval(refresh, 1000) at :1957), so every card node is destroyed and recreated once a second. .task-list is a scroll container (index.html:46) and nothing sets overflow-anchor, so the browser default of auto applies. Confirmed at runtime: getComputedStyle(list).overflowAnchor === "auto". Each tick the anchor node is destroyed, anchoring re-selects against entirely new nodes, and applies a positive adjustment.

Worth correcting the original theory: the client has no scroll tracking to get wrong. The only scroll code is combobox positioning (index.html:663, 669) and a scrollIntoView for keyboard navigation (:734). This is the browser compensating for churn, not the app miscalculating.

## Evidence

- Mechanism. Default anchoring drifted 2994 to 3578 over 8 ticks (delta 584). Setting overflow-anchor none on .task-list held 2994 across all 8 ticks (delta 0).
- Trigger. With polling frozen and no DOM edits, scrollTop held exactly at 2994. Calling replaceChildren with byte-identical clones, no data change at all, drifted 472 px over 6 iterations. Node-identity churn alone is sufficient.
- Node reuse. Editing text in place on existing nodes gave one legitimate 36 px adjustment then held steady across five further iterations.

## Work

Set overflow-anchor: none on .task-list in the stylesheet (internal/webui/assets/index.html:46). One line, measured to fully stop the drift.

Keep this declaration permanently even after the reconciling renderer lands, as a guard against any future code path that rebuilds a column reintroducing the drift silently.

## Acceptance

- A column scrolled to an arbitrary position holds it across at least ten consecutive polls with no user interaction.
- A poll that genuinely changes a columns contents still updates it.
- The declaration carries a short comment naming what it defends against, so it is not removed later as apparently dead styling.

Regression coverage lives with the structural fix, because the property worth asserting is node identity across a render, which the fake-DOM harness can observe and which this CSS change does not provide. Note the existing handler_test.go references at :1013-1023 to top, middle, and bottom scroll position are combobox placement cases, not board scrolling.
